profile.campus: Google Northern Virginia (Reston / Loudoun County / Prince William County), VA
profile.reading:
This building is part of Google's Northern Virginia data center footprint, mapped near Arcola, Loudoun County, one of several OSM-mapped buildings in this immediate area. Google's own Virginia locations page, fetched this session, does not name individual buildings or addresses within its Northern Virginia footprint, so this specific structure is not independently identified beyond its OSM-derived location.

Google's cloud infrastructure operates as a business of Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL/GOOG, SEC CIK 0001652044), headquartered at 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, California. Google's own Virginia data center location page, fetched fresh this session, states the company established a Virginia presence in 2009, purchased Northern Virginia land in 2017, opened its first facility in 2019, expanded a second Loudoun County facility in 2021, and opened a third in Prince William County in 2023; in 2025 Google announced a $9 billion investment for 2025-2026 spanning existing Northern Virginia sites and a new Chesterfield County campus. Google reports $15.6 billion in Virginia economic activity and over 36,000 employee volunteer hours since 2010.

Northern Virginia's Data Center Alley corridor, of which this Arcola-area building is part, hosts large single-tenant campuses for AWS and Meta and colocation operators including Digital Realty and Equinix, all separately tracked in this registry, though Google's own public materials describe its Virginia footprint in aggregate rather than naming individual buildings or per-building capacity figures.

Loudoun and Prince William counties sit at the center of what industry trackers call Data Center Alley, the largest concentration of data center capacity in the world by aggregate power draw, a status Loudoun County's own economic development office has cited in public materials for over a decade. Dominion Energy, the regional utility, has repeatedly flagged this corridor in integrated resource plan filings with the Virginia State Corporation Commission as the single largest driver of new electricity demand in its Virginia service territory, prompting new transmission and generation investment. Virginia's data center sales-and-use tax exemption, administered by the Virginia Economic Development Partnership and renewed by the General Assembly, has been a material factor in Google and other hyperscalers continuing to expand in the corridor rather than building only in lower-tax states, though Google has not disclosed how much exemption value this specific facility has claimed.

reading.body:
This building in Arcola, Loudoun County, is one of several structures within Google's Northern Virginia data center footprint, a campus Google describes in aggregate rather than by individual building. Google does not publish a megawatt IT capacity figure for this specific structure, so its size relative to other facilities cannot be determined from operator specifications. The building's role in Google's Virginia operations is confirmed, but its distinct capacity and purpose within the campus are not publicly stated.

Northern Virginia, anchored by the Loudoun County corridor known as Data Center Alley, is the largest data center market in the world by aggregate capacity. Google operates here alongside AWS, Meta, Digital Realty, and Equinix, all in the same corridor tracked by this registry. Dominion Energy, the regional utility, has flagged data center demand as the single largest driver of new electricity consumption in its Virginia service territory, a constraint that applies to this facility as part of the broader Northern Virginia buildout.

Among Virginia's 330 mapped data center facilities, only 23 operators publish megawatt figures, totaling 1,375.4 MW statewide. This Arcola building cannot be ranked within that published set because Google does not disclose per-building capacity. Virginia's sales-and-use tax exemption for data center equipment, administered by the state economic development authority, has been credited by local officials as material to continued hyperscaler expansion in this corridor, though the exemption value claimed by this specific facility is not published.
